spans.text: In 1989, Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web (see the original proposal).

contextSpans.text: He coined the term "World Wide Web," wrote the first World Wide Web server, "httpd," and the first client program (a browser and editor), "WorldWideWeb," in October 1990.

spans.context: In 1989, Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web (see the original proposal). He coined the term "World Wide Web," wrote the first World Wide Web server, "httpd," and the first client program (a browser and editor), "WorldWideWeb," in October 1990.

spans.text: In November 1990, this “web of information nodes in which the user can browse at will” was formalised as a proposal, “WorldWideWeb: Proposal for a HyperText Project”, by Berners-Lee, together with a CERN colleague, Robert Cailliau.

contextSpans.text: Sir Tim Berners-Lee’s first proposal in March 1989 was for an internet-based hypertext system to link and access information across different computers.
